messages.subject: multilevel multigroup model errors
parts:
Hello,

I am running a multilevel multigroup model comparing effects b/w younger and older siblings (“Birth Order”), accounting for nesting within families (“FamID”).
My code is replicated below:

model = ‘
Group: 1
Level: 1
   IT2 ~ S1 + SibSupport + S1xSibSupport + IT1
Level: 2
   IT2 ~ FamID

Group: 1
Level: 1
   IT2 ~ S1 + SibSupport + S1xSibSupport + IT1
Level: 2
   IT2 ~ FamID’

modelfit = sem(model=model, data=data, missing=“FIML”, estimator=“MLR”, group=“BirthOrder”, cluster=“FamID”)


Is this the correct specification for level 2? All variables are at level 1.

Errors from running the above code are:
Error in if (fx.delta < tol) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning message:
In lav_partable_check(lavpartable, categorical = lavoptions$categorical,  :
  lavaan WARNING: automatically added intercepts are set to zero:
    [IT2]


Any help would be appreciated! Thanks!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: multilevel multigroup model errors
parts: I am running a multilevel multigroup model comparing effects b/w younger and older siblings (“Birth Order”), accounting for nesting within families (“FamID”).

I don't think lavaan can do this.  Your grouping variable varies within clusters/families (Level 1).  The block structure in lavaan syntax in your MG-ML-SEM assumes the grouping variable is constant within clusters (Level 2).

It might be possible to implement MuML estimation in lavaan with a Level-1 grouping variable, but I have not implemented it, so please report back here if you are able to accomplish it.  Advantageously, it sounds like you have equal cluster sizes (2 siblings per family?), which MuML assumes.  This paper has the details:

https://doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2014.1003769

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
